A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pareto Merging research by Chen and Kwok, despite the changed title. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging accuracies, unseen-task evaluations, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices 2–5, alongside baseline results attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic optimization results and model-merging experiments, including data-free variants, unseen-task evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v2 retains the preference-dependent low-rank tensor but adds data-free optimization using parameter-distance objectives and fixed merging weights, alongside entropy-based optimization with learned weights. It removes cosine regularization, changes the tensor penalty to the norm of its contraction with an all-ones vector, and replaces uniform Dirichlet sampling with configurable concentration, set to 0.1.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A add a synthetic two-objective optimization problem with a 6-by-6 matrix parameter. The eight image-classification datasets and both held-out task pairs remain unchanged; the new data-free variants use these existing classification tasks.

E2.justification: DARE and MAP enter the eight-model comparisons for both backbones. The two-model evaluation now compares against Rewarded Soups and MAP, while the earlier AdaMerging + Preference control is absent. AdaMerging++ becoming AdaMerging + TIES is only a renaming.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the random-preference examples with systematic priority reporting, assigning 0.5 to the prioritized task and 0.5/7 to each other task, while retaining equal preferences. It removes the 36-preference three-model experiment and adds a 31-preference toy protocol. New MAP settings include a population of 100 and nested merging; reported regularization and preference-sampling defaults also change.

E4.justification: The cosine-weight and tensor-regularization sensitivity studies in v1 Appendix 4 disappear. Rank sensitivity and the tensor-versus-outer-product comparison remain with revised results in v2 Section 4.3 and Appendix E. The new toy study additionally checks learned Pareto-front coverage against a ground-truth front.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Multiple sampled preferences represent different models, not statistical repetitions.

E6.justification: Many numerical results and plotted solutions change, with new data-free, priority-preference, MAP, DARE, and toy results, and removal of three-model and random-preference results. For example, equal-preference entropy-based PM averages 92.0 on ViT-L/14 in v1 Table 8 versus 91.2 in v2 Table 6. Task Arithmetic's unseen-SVHN entry changes from 44.9 to 49.9, now matching the retained average of 51.1. Revised PM results accompany changed objectives and settings, so they are not controlled version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.1 adds a squared-distance formulation and closed-form derivation for data-free merging, identifying Task Arithmetic and Rewarded Soups as special cases. Appendix A also defines the synthetic objectives. The existing Pareto definitions and smooth-Tchebycheff optimality statement remain; no new general convergence or optimality proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The claimed applicability expands from the unlabeled-data, entropy-based merger in v1 to a framework augmenting both data-free and unlabeled-data merging methods in v2. This substantially broadens the contribution's scope. The central claims of preference-aware model generation through one optimization process with small storage overhead remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about overfitting at large ranks and warns that apparent dominance in two-dimensional projections need not hold in eight dimensions. Appendix C also explains why extreme trade-offs may be undesirable. The earlier detailed interpretations of cosine-controlled diversity and tensor regularization's interaction with entropy optimization are removed.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly documents use of official baseline implementations and Task Arithmetic's validation search over merging weights, including the selected values. Appendix A supplies toy initialization, rank, and optimizer settings. Most checkpoint, optimizer, batch-size, hardware, and software details are retained. Newly disclosed baseline settings do not establish that those settings changed from v1.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around Rewarded Soups and MAP, comparing storage, data requirements, and continuous versus discrete Pareto-set representations. It adds discussion of DARE, task-specific merging approaches, LORPMAN, and additional MOO methods, and explicitly claims the first use of gradient-based MOO for model merging.

P1.justification: Beyond the new title, substantial method, background, and experimental passages are rewritten and reorganized. The methodology separates data-free and unlabeled-data cases; experiments separate toy and real-world studies; variant names become base-method-plus-PM combinations. Appendix organization changes, and the rank discussion moves into the main text.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show the shared base, low-rank component, and user-specific outputs. Comparison tables gain grouped equal/priority rows and shading; the timing table adds parameter and model counts. The three-model figure disappears, new toy and data-free plots appear, and figures are resized or relocated within a changed document layout. v2 Figure 7 enlarges Figure 3 rather than reporting another experiment.

improvement.justification: Direct comparisons with preference-aware MAP and Rewarded Soups, explicit storage/runtime measurements, and additional baseline implementation details make v2's empirical positioning more informative. The data-free extension also receives supporting experiments. However, the earlier AdaMerging + Preference control is removed, and the revised tensor regularizer lacks the sensitivity analysis available in v1. These losses limit the net quality gain; changed accuracies alone do not establish improvement.
